subject: Compression sprint & MAP revision — close date contingency
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: initial timeline + gating items

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've pulled the team together and sketched a tentative MAP. A couple of early flags:

- Procurement has a standing review window the week of Feb 8 that will block PO issuance until after their vendor security review completes.
- Our security team has requested SOC2 artifacts and live log access for an evaluator before we sign off on a go-live date.

I've attached a draft MAP (MAP-draft.xlsx) showing the current target close of Feb 25. Realistically, procurement + security review will push us ~10 business days unless we can accelerate steps in parallel.

Can your team share the SOC2 evidence and an audit-log retention statement? Also curious if Redwood can commit to a short-term capacity hold in case we need to shift the close by a few days.

Best,
Alex
Account Exec, Acme Corp
alex.jones@acme.com

Attachment: MAP-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: initial timeline + gating items

Alex —

Appreciate the heads-up and the MAP draft. Quick responses and options from our side:

1) Evidence: Ben is pulling a SOC2 snapshot and audit log summary. We can share redacted artifacts by EOD tomorrow and a read-only link for your security reviewer.
2) Capacity: We can hold a temporary dedicated slot (no extra cost for up to 7 days) if you provide a soft commitment date by Feb 10.
3) Parallel eval: We recommend running the security checklist in parallel with procurement review — this can usually shave off ~7 business days.

If procurement insists on a firm PO before exposure to logs, option 2 is the safest. I've looped Marissa to flag a quick commercial concession if the PO timeline slips.

Next steps: confirm whether your security team will accept redacted audit logs and the name of the procurement contact so we can coordinate.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: initial timeline + gating items

Alex / Team,

I attached a short risk log below (summary) and will provide the artifact bundle by tomorrow noon.

Risk log (summary):
- R1: Procurement hold — Medium — Impact: Close +10 business days if PO/approval delayed.
- R2: Security eval requests live log access — High — Impact: gating until read-only access accepted.
- R3: Capacity contention — Low — We can reserve a slot for short windows; long holds require a commit.

Mitigations:
- Provide redacted audit logs + SOC2 artefacts (attachment: SOC2-evidence.pdf)
- Offer a staged rollout: dev-only pass, followed by production "soft" cutover with guardrails
- If procurement needs a hard close date, request a 30-day acceptance window with automatic extension clauses

Alex, please confirm which mitigations procurement will accept so we can update the MAP and surface any commercial levers.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-evidence.pdf (document stub)

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: initial timeline + gating items

Evelyn / Ben,

Quick update from our side: procurement confirmed their vendor security review kicks off Feb 8 and will not issue a PO until the review closes. That review typically runs 7–10 business days. Legal also wants final T&Cs signed before any capacity reservations.

This pushes our internal target considerably — we're now looking at a close window in mid-March unless Redwood can (a) provide an auditable read-only log link now, or (b) commit to a temporary reservation and a separate contract to be executed post-PO.

Procure@acme.com has asked for a short summary of what Redwood will provide during the security review and whether there are standard contractual fallback terms for delayed acceptance.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: initial timeline + gating items — proposed compression sprint

Alex,

Thanks for the update and for surfacing procurement's timing. Below is a concrete 'compression sprint' plan to keep you in the Feb window or, at minimum, minimize the slip to a single two-week bump.

Option A — Parallel security + procurement (preferred):
- Redwood provides redacted audit logs + SOC2 snapshot today (Ben attached).
- Schedule a 45-minute security Q&A with our infra team (we can do Fri Feb 12 or Mon Feb 15).
- If security confirms a read-only review is acceptable, procurement can continue in parallel; target close Feb 25 stands.

Option B — Capacity reservation + conditional contract:
- Redwood holds a dedicated capacity slot for 10 business days from Feb 22.
- We will issue a conditional SOW and attach a DocuSign link; production activation contingent on PO within that window.
- If PO arrives after the window, capacity may be released but we will prioritize reallocation.

Option C — Staged acceptance (lowest risk):
- Dev-only go-live on Feb 25 with production toggle.
- 30-day acceptance window that begins at soft-go-live; final billing and SLA commence on completion of acceptance tests.

Commercial concession: Marissa, can we offer a 10% credits package if Acme signs the PO and accepts the staged acceptance terms? If yes, I'll include in the updated MAP.

I'll prepare MAP-v2.xlsx with the selected mitigations and a short exec summary for procure@acme.com. Links below include the HubSpot record and a temp DocuSign skeleton.

Proposed next step: Alex — pick A/B/C and confirm your procurement contact's acceptance criteria. If we don't hear back by Feb 16 we'll proceed with Option B reservation.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx
Related links: https://hubspot.example.com/contacts/1234567, https://docu.sign/ABCDEF123456
